newsitem.title: USA: Waste Recovery sets Wisconsin pact.
newsitem.headline: Waste Recovery sets Wisconsin pact.

text.p: Waste Recovery Inc said Thursday it had signed an agreement with Wisconsin Power & Light Co, a subsidiary of WPL Holdings Inc, to supply the electric utility with tire-derived fuel for a period of one year beginning in January.
Under the agreement, Waste Recovery will deliver to Wisconsin P&L a minimum of 19,500 tons of the fuel, it said. This is the equivalent of some 2.5 million tires, it said.

"For the first time since the opening of our Marseilles plant in northern Illinois, we will be able to produce TDF (tire-derived fuel) at this facility and ship it directly to a major customer for fuel consumption," said Waste Recovery Chief Executive Thomas Earnshaw.

"Currently, we pre-process the scrap tires at Marseilles and ship them to Dupo, our other Illinois facility, which is located in the St. Louis metropolitan area, for final processing before shipment to NIPSCO Industries Inc's Illinois Power."
"This new contract will now raise our capacity utilization rate in Illinois to about 70 percent, up from our current level of 50 percent," he said.
